multi.reason: n=18 against minPublishableN=30, so the suppression scripts/permits/denver.mjs applied is CONFIRMED CORRECT rather than assumed correct — 18 is measured, not estimated. HISTORY, because how this number was obtained is part of what it means: the 2026-08-06 run dropped the tier with a console warning and wrote nothing to this file, so the count that run saw was unrecoverable FROM THAT RUN, and this record was hand-populated 2026-08-09 stating the exact n as unknown. A re-probe on 2026-08-10 recovered it as 18. The 'exact n is unknown' wording that stood here until 2026-08-10 was true when written and is now false; it is retracted, not softened. Why the aggregate must not stand in (unchanged by the recovery): of newConstruction n=6,922, single accounts for 3,505 and apartment for 628, leaving 2,789 rows in neither published tier — the untiered residential rows (Denver's residential layer carries no UNITS value on many rows, including garages, carports, sheds and ADUs) plus the whole commercial layer. Just 18 of the 6,922 are 2-4 unit buildings. Serving 4.5 months to a duplex query was answering from a population that almost entirely excludes duplexes.

newConstruction.vintage: applied 2023-08-01 onward; computed 2026-08-06; NashvilleOpenData Building Permits Issued (ArcGIS Building_Permits_Issued_2 layer 0; Per_Ty IN (CARN, CACN, CACH) = Building Residential/Commercial - New + Commercial Shell, gated to building Per_SubTy only). Feed is a ROLLING ~3-YEAR window of ISSUED permits (2023-08-01..2026-08-04), so the 2022-01-01 start used for other cities is not attainable without left-truncation bias and 2023-08-01 is the earliest filing cohort the window covers completely. Because only issued permits appear, the issuance rate is not computable and this median is a FLOOR. Nashville also issues per-unit child permits under a master permit (24.9% of rows cite one), which re-weights the median toward large repetitive developments.

tierBreakdown.reason: scripts/permits/philadelphia.mjs computes no tier split. Its query filters on permitdescription (Residential/Commercial Building Permit) and typeofwork (New Construction*) — no size restriction — so the aggregate spans all three tiers.

newConstruction.vintage: applied 2022-01-01 onward; computed 2026-08-09; City of Raleigh ArcGIS Building_Permits layer 0 (workclass IN (New Building, New Residential Dwelling, Townhouse, Shell Building), gated to building proposeduse only). The feed carries NON-ISSUED applications, so this is close to an unconditional median rather than a floor: 90.7% of filings in the window have issued, and the matured 2022 and 2023 cohorts are at 97.3% and 97.4%. THE ROW IS NOT THE PROJECT — Raleigh issues per-unit child permits for townhomes (51% of the sample; 96.9% of those rows duplicate another row's description) and per-building child permits within larger developments (15.8% of apartment-tier rows cite a main case), which re-weights the median toward large repetitive developments. Townhouse rows are in the aggregate but carry no tier: the feed records neither the development's unit count nor a development id, so 'multi' vs 'apartment' is a GAP.
